title: Lamentation of the Homeless
text:
Forgive me, friend, I did not mean to bother you

but I came back from Vietnam

where I killed a lot of Vietnamese gentlemen

some ladies too

and I could not bear the pain

and out of fear I picked up a habit

and I went through rehab and I am clean

but I have nowhere to sleep

and I do not know what to do

with myself right now


I am sorry, friend, I did not mean to bother you

but it is cold in the street

and my heart is sick alone

and I am clean, but my life is a disaster

Third Avenue

and E. Houston Street

in the crosswalk under the red light

I clean your windshield with a dirty rag
editorial_note: The translation keeps the street address, confessional rush, and blunt veteran's voice of the provided text.

title: Good Luck
text:
I am lucky to have the five fingers on my right hand

Lucky to pee without it hurting too much

Lucky that the bowels move.

Lucky, I sleep at night in a captain's bed, midafternoon nap

Lucky to walk down First Avenue

Lucky to make a couple hundred thousand a year

singing Eli Eli, writing whatever passes through my head,

recording primordial scribbles,

teaching at a Buddhist college,

taking Leica photos of the bus stop

through the window of my eyes

I hear ambulance sirens, smell garlic and urine, taste loquats and sole,

walk barefoot across the loft floor, the soles of my feet somewhat numb

Lucky that I can think and that the sky can snow
editorial_note: The translation keeps the gratitude list's bodily comedy and New York specificity.

title: The Bright Intelligence
text:
Emigrate from death

to make a sign of Life again in You

fierce and beautiful as a car accident

in the Plaza de Armas


I swear I have seen that light

I will not stop kissing your cheeks

when they close your coffin

And the mourning humans return to their old

and tired dream.

And you wake in the Eye of the Dictator

of the Universe


Another stupid miracle! Again I am wrong!

Your indifference! My enthusiasm!

I insist! You cough!

Lost in the Gold-Wave floating

through the Cosmos.


Ah I am tired of insisting! Goodbye

I am going to Pucalpa

to have visions.

Your clean sonnets?


I want your secret drafts

dirtier

your hope,

in its most obscene Magnificence, oh God!
editorial_note: The translation preserves the breathless exclamations and spiritual sarcasm of the Spanish source.

title: Envoi
text:
The song you asked me for,

I composed it and here it is;

sing it low and sadly:

she sleeps (forever); the song will lull her.


Sing it low and sadly,

sing it...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the lullaby restraint and the parenthetical forever.

editorial_note: This related version preserves the same brief song while retaining its catalog title.

title: The Most Natural Thing
text:
You left me —as you were passing by—

the most immaterial thing, which is your gaze.


I left you —as I was in such haste—

the most immaterial thing, which is my smile.


But between your gaze and my smiling

face the same dream remained floating.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the small exchange of gaze and smile as shared dream.

title: The Squirrel
text:
The squirrel runs.

The squirrel flies.

The squirrel jumps

like a little madcap.

—Mother, does the squirrel

not go to school?

—Come, little squirrel,

I have a cage

that is very pretty.

—No, I prefer

my tree trunk

and my hole.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the children's poem simplicity and the squirrel's free answer.

title: En Panne
text:
Stuffed with philosophy,

because of the eagerness that devours me,

I, who already knew

two grams of living, know nothing now.


From asking so much

the road from the wise men who passed,

I was left without arriving,

while so many fools arrived...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the wry complaint that too much inquiry stopped arrival.
